01.actor: Rav Ashi, with Ameimar and Mar Zutra
01.event: While the sages sat at King Izgur's gate, a butler passed with food and Rav Ashi saw Mar Zutra's face go pale with craving, so he put some of the food in Mar Zutra's mouth.
01.turn: The butler objected that the king's meal was spoiled; Rav Ashi said the food itself was spoiled and pointed to a spot the soldiers had not checked.
01.outcome: They checked that spot and found a leprous infection; Rav Ashi explained that he had seen a leprous spirit hovering over the food.
01.summary: Three sages sat at the king's gate as the royal butler passed with food. Rav Ashi saw Mar Zutra go pale with craving and fed him some with his finger. The butler complained that he had ruined the king's meal, but Rav Ashi said the food was already unfit and pointed to a spot nobody had checked. They looked there and found the infection, and Rav Ashi said he had seen a leprous spirit over it.

02.missing: Rava's and Abaye's legal argument about two identically named people; the promissory-note case is cited only as a proof.

03.event: A man deposited a silver goblet with Ḥasa, who died without saying anything about it, and the depositor's claim came before Rav Naḥman.
03.turn: Rav Naḥman said he knew Ḥasa was not wealthy and the claimant had given a distinguishing mark.
03.outcome: He ruled for the claimant, with the caveat that this holds only if the claimant did not regularly come and go in the house.
03.summary: A man left a silver goblet in the house of Ḥasa, who then died without leaving instructions. The depositor came before Rav Naḥman to claim it. Rav Naḥman said he knew Ḥasa was not wealthy and the claimant could describe the goblet, so the claimant was believed, unless he regularly visited the house.

04.missing: Only a bare report that two sages recited different numbers of blessings at weddings; no event, turn or end.

05.actor: Rabbi Tarfon, Rabbi Akiva and the Elders
05.event: Gathered in a loft in Lod, the sages were asked whether study or action is greater and each answered.
05.turn: Tarfon said action, Akiva said study, and then all agreed study is greater.
05.outcome: They concluded study is greater because it leads to action.
05.summary: Rabbi Tarfon and the Elders were reclining in a loft in Lod when someone asked whether study or action is greater. Tarfon said action and Akiva said study, and then everyone agreed study is greater because it leads to action.
05.missing: It is a scene of a question and answers; there is no action beyond the exchange.

06.event: Rav Ashi knew testimony relevant to Rav Kahana, but when Rav Kahana asked if he remembered it, Rav Ashi said no, then recalled it and testified.
06.turn: Rav Kahana looked hesitant, suspecting he had planted the memory.
06.outcome: Rav Ashi said he was not relying on Rav Kahana, and had made an effort to remember on his own.
06.summary: Rav Ashi knew testimony that mattered to Rav Kahana. Rav Kahana asked if he remembered it, and Rav Ashi said no, even when prompted with details. Eventually Rav Ashi remembered and testified for him. Seeing that Rav Kahana hesitated, Rav Ashi said he was not relying on him but had made an effort and remembered on his own.

07.missing: Abaye and Rava debating how to permit carrying in a yard; a legal problem-solving discussion, no event.

08.event: Rav Kahana held an orphan's beer and delayed selling it until the Festival.
08.turn: He reasoned that although it might sour a little, it would fetch cash at the Festival.
08.summary: Rav Kahana was holding beer that belonged to an orphan, Rav Mesharshiyya. He held off selling it until the Festival, reasoning that even if it soured slightly it would bring a better price in cash then.
08.missing: No result of the delay is stated; it is a reported decision with its rationale.

09.actor: Mari bar Isak and the brother who came to him
09.event: A man claiming to be Mari's brother came from a distant district and demanded a share of the father's estate; Mari said he did not know him.
09.turn: Rav Ḥisda backed Mari because a brother may not be recognized after years, then demanded the claimant bring witnesses; the claimant said they feared Mari, so Rav Ḥisda told Mari to bring witnesses that he was not his brother.
09.outcome: Mari objected that the burden is on the claimant; Rav Ḥisda said that is how he judges violent men.
09.summary: A man from a faraway district came to Mari bar Isak, said he was his brother and asked for a share of their father's estate. Mari said he did not know him, and they went to Rav Ḥisda. Rav Ḥisda first said Mari's denial was reasonable, then told the claimant to bring witnesses; he said they were afraid of Mari. So Rav Ḥisda told Mari to prove the man was not his brother, and when Mari protested, he said this is how he treats violent men.

10.actor: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai and the daughter of Nakdimon ben Guryon
10.event: Riding out of Jerusalem, Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai saw a young woman picking barley from Arab animals' dung, who wrapped herself in her hair and begged him for sustenance.
10.turn: She revealed she was Nakdimon's daughter and reminded him he had signed her marriage contract, which promised a huge dowry.
10.outcome: He wept and said Israel is fortunate when it does God's will, and that otherwise it is handed even to the animals of a lowly nation.
10.summary: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai, riding out of Jerusalem with his students, saw a young woman gathering barley from animal dung, covering herself with her hair. He did not recognize her until she said she was Nakdimon ben Guryon's daughter and that wealth had been lost. She reminded him he had signed her marriage contract, which promised a million gold dinars. He wept and said that when Israel does not do God's will, it is delivered even to the animals of a lowly nation.

11.event: Neḥemya was so absorbed in study that he walked beyond the Shabbat limit.
11.turn: Rav Ḥisda told Rav Naḥman that Neḥemya was in distress, stuck outside the limit.
11.outcome: Rav Naḥman advised making a human partition so that Neḥemya could walk back in.
11.summary: Neḥemya, son of Rav Ḥanilai, got so lost in his studies that he walked beyond the Shabbat limit without noticing. Rav Ḥisda told Rav Naḥman that Neḥemya was in distress. Rav Naḥman answered that people should line up to form a human wall, letting him walk back inside.

12.actor: A childless woman and Rabbi Ami
12.event: A woman came to Rabbi Ami asking for her marriage contract payment and divorce because her husband could not father children.
12.turn: He sent her away since women are not commanded to procreate; she replied that in old age she would have no one to look after her.
12.outcome: Rabbi Ami ruled that in such a case the husband is certainly forced to divorce her.
12.summary: A woman came before Rabbi Ami asking for her marriage contract money, wanting a divorce from her childless husband. He told her to go away since she was not commanded to have children. She asked who would care for her in old age, and Rabbi Ami agreed that in that case the husband is forced to divorce her.

13.actor: A man who longed for a woman, in Eretz Yisrael
13.event: He was suffering over a woman and wanted to leave Eretz Yisrael, but on hearing the teaching about the merit of living there, he stayed.
13.turn: Hearing the statement about Eretz Yisrael changed his intent to leave.
13.outcome: He remained, suffering, until the day he died.
13.summary: Rabba's brothers wrote him from Eretz Yisrael with an incident. A man was suffering over a woman and wanted to leave the Land. When he heard the idea about the tremendous significance of living there, he stayed and suffered until he died.
13.missing: The idea he heard and the full context of the letter; the rest of the passage is advice.

14.event: A reservoir in Yavne presumed to hold forty se'a was measured and found short, and the two sages disagreed about purifications done in it.
14.turn: Tarfon declared them pure and Akiva impure; they traded parables of priests, and Tarfon proposed deciding by which case it resembles.
14.outcome: Akiva argued the reservoir resembles the blemished priest, not the son of a divorced woman, and Tarfon said whoever separates from Akiva separates from life.
14.summary: A reservoir in Yavne thought to be full was measured and found deficient. Rabbi Tarfon ruled all purifications done in it were still pure, while Rabbi Akiva said they were impure. They argued with parables about priests, and Akiva showed the reservoir was like a blemished priest, not the son of a divorced woman. Tarfon accepted this, saying that whoever separates from Akiva separates from life.

15.actor: Rava, his wife (the daughter of Rav Ḥisda), and a woman obligated to swear
15.event: A woman was obligated to take an oath in Rava's court, and Rava's wife said she knew the woman was untrustworthy about oaths.
15.turn: Rava was told the woman could not be trusted to swear truthfully.
15.outcome: Rava reversed the oath onto the opposing party.
15.summary: A woman was required to take an oath in Rava's court. Rava's wife, the daughter of Rav Ḥisda, told him she knew the woman was not reliable about oaths. Rava then shifted the obligation to swear onto the other party.

16.missing: A legal answer using an observation about Mar Shmuel and the Neharde'a gateways, offered as proof; no story.

17.event: Rav Ḥisda's daughter asked whether he wished to sleep a little, since he spent his nights studying.
17.turn: He answered that long days of being dead would soon come, with plenty of sleep.
17.summary: Rav Ḥisda's daughter asked her father, who studied through the night, if he did not want to sleep a little. He said days would soon come that are long but short in opportunity, in which he would sleep a great deal.
17.missing: It is a brief exchange with no consequence or ending.

18.event: Ravina arranged his son's marriage to a woman from Rav Ḥaviva's house and recited the betrothal blessing, confident they would not retract.
18.summary: Ravina arranged a match for his son with a woman from Rav Ḥaviva's household and recited the blessing from the time of betrothal, sure they would not back out. But the matter did not work out and they retracted, so the wedding did not happen.

19.actor: A man who sold land to Rav Pappa
19.event: A man sold land to Rav Pappa because he needed money to buy oxen.
19.turn: Eventually he no longer needed the money and wanted his land back.
19.outcome: Rav Pappa returned the land to him, going beyond the letter of the law.
19.summary: A man sold land to Rav Pappa in order to raise money for oxen. In the end he did not need the money after all. Rav Pappa returned the land to him, though the Gemara says he did so beyond what the law required.

20.missing: First-person remarks of sages that they would have suffered had food not been shared, ending in a general principle; no single event retold.
